kept.title: Change from path.join to url.resolve breaks asset path behavior
kept.explanation: The previous implementation returned the asset path as a file path joined by path.join(post.path, this.slug), treating it as a relative file path. The new code uses url.resolve(post.path, this.slug), which performs URL resolution. This changes the path semantics and may produce unexpected URLs, especially if post.path or slug contain special characters or slashes. This breaks the expected file-path-relative-to-public_dir behavior documented in the original code, causing assets to resolve incorre
kept.suggestion: Revert the change to use path.join(post.path, this.slug) to preserve the original path resolution semantics.
kept.failureAfterChange: Any post.path like '/foo/' with slug 'bar' would produce an unexpected URL from url.resolve, not a proper relative file path. Asset URLs may become incorrect or broken in generated content.

verdicts.reason: The finding identifies a concrete defect introduced by the change: replacing path.join with url.resolve alters the semantics of asset path resolution, potentially breaking URL generation as per the original intent and comment in the code. This is a valid defect introduced by the change.
